title: 20. Virtual fencing is as effective as polywire for strip grazing stockpiled sorghum–sudangrass.
content:
Abstract
The objective of this 2-yr study was to evaluate the efficacy of virtual fencing for managing strip grazing of stockpiled sorghum–sudangrass based forage compared with traditional temporary electric fencing, and to compare strip grazing with continuous grazing. In each year, growing steers (262.61 ± 0.33 kg; n = 60) were stratified by weight and assigned to one of three grazing treatments: continuous grazing (CONT), strip grazing with polywire electric fence (POLY), or strip grazing using eShepherd virtual fencing collars (VF). Each yr a field was divided into six equal paddocks (1.82 and 1.58 ha in yr 1 and 2, respectively), and randomly assigned to treatments, with two replicates per treatment per yr and 10 steers per paddock. Strip-grazed paddocks (POLY and VF) were subdivided into 0.23 ha strips, with new forage allocated every 9.5 ± 1.2 d. All steers received 1.1 kg DM/d of dried distillers grains, delivered three times per week. Grazing was terminated when forage availability became limiting in CONT, resulting in 54 and 59 grazing days in yr 1 and 2, respectively. At the end of grazing, strip-grazed treatments utilized 1.36 ha in both years, representing 75 and 85% of the land area used by CONT in yr 1 and 2, respectively. Data were analyzed as a completely randomized design using PROC mixed in SAS 9.4 and paddock was experimental unit. Grazing treatment and year were included as fixed effects. There was a treatment by year interaction (P < 0.01) for carrying capacity (AUM/ha), however, within year, CONT was less (P < 0.01) than POLY and VF, which did not differ (P ≥ 0.13). Mean carrying capacity across both years was 6.94, 8.56, 8.51 AUM/ha (SEM ± 0.0259 ) for CONT, POLY and VF, respectively. There were no other treatment by year interactions (P ≥ 0.25). There was no treatment effect (P = 0.21; SEM ±0.02) for ADG at 0.64 kg in CONT, 0.63 kg in POLY and 0.59 kg in VF. Gain per hectare of CONT (236 ± 8.25 kg/ha) was lesser (P = 0.02) than POLY (275± 8.25 kg/ha) with VF being intermediate (258 ± 8.25 kg/ha) not differing from CONT (P = 0.11) or POLY (P = 0.21). Overall, strip grazing did not impact individual animal performance but ?show $132#?>increased carrying capacity by 13-24%. These results suggest VF is equally effective as polywire fencing for strip-grazing management and has the potential to reduce labor requirements.
